intervals.label: underground installation and cooldown at Soudan
intervals.note: End: data taking started on 4 December 2009 ('spanning 442 live days over the period 4 December 2009 to 6 March 2011', arXiv:1208.5737). The 2013 paper says the detector was 'installed in the Soudan Underground Laboratory (SUL) during 2009'.
intervals.quote: Underground installation of this PPC at SUL took place on August 21, 2009.

intervals.label: initial run (442 live days to 6 March 2011)
intervals.note: Month precision for the end: the data set ends 6 March 2011 and a fire in the access shaft halted the run in March 2011.
intervals.quote: spanning 442 live days over the period 4 December 2009 to 6 March 2011

intervals.label: outage after the Soudan access-shaft fire
intervals.note: Start: month precision ('halted the initial run in March of 2011', arXiv:1208.5737); end: 7 June 2011 ('three month downtime').
intervals.quote: Operation restarted on 7 June 2011 following a three month downtime.

intervals.label: continuous data taking after the fire (data set analysed to 23 April 2013)
intervals.note: Open interval: the detector 'has taken data continuously since' 7 June 2011 and the latest data set read ends 23 April 2013 (1,129 live days of the 1,237-day span; the maximum-likelihood paper quotes 1136 live days). No source read states when, or whether, CoGeNT stopped: the January 2014 paper still says 'The CoGeNT detector presently operating at the Soudan Underground Laboratory', the C-4 upgrade was described as ongoing, and the Atlas's Soudan facility record has the laboratory decommissioning from 2016. The status 'active' is therefore a last-known state, not a 2026 observation.
intervals.quote: The presently examined cumulative dataset ends on 23 April 2013, spanning 1,237 days, of which 1,129 were live.

placements.note: CoGeNT sat in the Soudan-2 (proton-decay) hall: the PRD paper says its shield rests on 'base I-beams that once supported the Soudan-2 proton decay experiment' at 2090 m.w.e., whereas the Atlas's only Soudan site is the MINOS far-detector cavern (2070 m.w.e.). They are different halls of the same mine level; no source read gives the Soudan-2 hall's coordinates, so the MINOS-cavern point stands for the laboratory.
placements.quote: The present CoGeNT detector is located at the Soudan Underground Laboratory (Soudan, Minnesota, USA)

depth.quote: providing 2090 meters of water equivalent (m.w.e.) overburden as shielding against cosmic rays

target_mass.quote: A new 440 g PPC diode was built with attention paid to these.

threshold.quote: down to the 0.4 keVee electronic noise threshold

summary.plain: CoGeNT ran a single 440-gram germanium crystal in the Soudan mine in Minnesota to look for very light dark matter. It reported an unexplained excess of low-energy events and a seasonal rate change that fit light dark matter, but called their origin unknown and the significance low, and other experiments did not confirm them.
summary.technical: Single modified BEGe p-type point-contact germanium diode (440 g; ~0.4 keVee noise threshold) in a Pb/Cu/polyethylene shield at Soudan (2090 m.w.e.), installed 21 Aug 2009, data from 4 Dec 2009. 2010 PRL: an irreducible excess of bulk-like events below 3 keVee. 2011 PRL (442 live days): a ~2.8 sigma annual modulation. 2013 PRD: detailed background model; no viable background explanation found. 2014: 3.4-year release (1,129 live days) with a modulation amplitude ~4-7 times the standard-halo expectation; maximum-likelihood significance 1.7 sigma, 'well below evidentiary'. An excess is not a discovery.

technology.quote: The detector element is a single modified BEGe germanium diode.
technology.value: Single modified BEGe p-type point-contact (PPC) germanium diode with sub-keV threshold
